chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Barqī, from Ibn Sinān or someone else, who raised it to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, our hadith is difficult, made difficult; none can bear it except enlightened breasts, or sound hearts, or good morals.
Indeed, Allah took the covenant from our Shiʿah just as He took it from the children of Ādam:
So whoever is faithful to us, Allah will fulfill for him with Paradise; and whoever hates us and does not render our right to us, then he will be in the Fire, abiding forever.

key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire as the punishment for enmity and failing their right
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقَ: the covenant or solemn pledge taken by Allah
key_terms.حَدِيثَنَا: the hadith and teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: the followers and adherents of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.صَعْبٌ مُسْتَصْعَبٌ: extremely difficult and demanding to comprehend or bear
key_terms.صُدُورٌ مُنِيرَةٌ: enlightened breasts, meaning inwardly illumined souls
key_terms.قُلُوبٌ سَلِيمَةٌ: sound and wholesome hearts free of corruption

ai.seo_question: Why are the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt considered difficult, and what is the reward for loyalty to them?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the teachings of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام are profound and can only be borne by those with inner illumination, sound hearts, and noble character. It links loyalty to them with the primordial covenant and describes ultimate reward or punishment in the afterlife according to one's fulfillment of their right.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Barqy, from Ibn Sinan, or someonle else, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Our<sup>asws</sup> Ahadeeth are difficult, becoming more difficult. None can bear it except for an enlightened chest, or a tranquil heart, or excellent morals.
Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Took the Covenant from our<sup>asws</sup> Shias just as He<sup>azwj</sup> Took upon the Children of Adam<sup>as</sup>
[7:172] Am I not your Lord?

So the one who was loyal to us<sup>asws</sup>, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Loyal to him with the Paradise, and the one who hates us<sup>asws</sup> and does not fulfill our<sup>asws</sup> rights to us<sup>asws</sup>, so in the Fire he will abide eternally’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Barqi from ibn Sinan or others in a marfu‘ manner from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Our Hadith (statements) are difficult and they become difficult. Only well lighted chests, the well protected of virtuous moral abilities are capable to accept them.”
Allah has taken a pledge from our Shi‘a (followers) just as He has taken such pledge from the children of Adam
Whoever would remain loyal to us Allah will grant then paradise. Whoever would dislike us and would not deliver our rights to us they will live in fire forever.”
